newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end up sharply on weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end up sharply on weather concerns.

text.p: Buying linked to talk of wintry weather expected to move through southern and central Plains feedlot areas next week and stepped up fed cattle sales pushed CME live cattle futures to day's highs by the close, traders said.

Live cattle ended 0.950 to 0.125 cent a lb higher with December pacing the gain and February up 0.775 at 63.700 cents. Feeder cattle finished 0.625 to 0.175 cent higher with January up most at 66.525 cents.
The forecast for snow to be followed by bitterly cold weather across the southern and central Plains sparked increased commercial buying interest late, traders said.

Adding to the strong tone was ideas of bottoming in boxed beef prices. This was further encouraged by reports that packers were picking up previously bought cattle early and would likely have to raise bids for more cattle next week. Choice boxed values slipped further at noon and sales remained active, they said.
"They (packers) will have to pay up for cattle next week to satisfy (beef) business they booked for the first of the year," said Jim Clarkson, analysts for A and A Inc.

In live cattle options, Dean Witter bought February 68 calls. There was commercial hedging in April and June, buying of puts and selling of calls. Late, commission houses sold February 62 calls, pit sources said.

Feeder cattle futures continued to follow the lead of live cattle and rose on local short covering, buy stops and commission house demand. An easy tone to corn futures and a higher CME feeder cattle index also lifted values during the day, traders said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.04 at $64.87 per cwt.

Cargill Investor Services spread long August/short October and Refco bought January and sold March with ADM Investor Services on the other side, traders said. Stone traders bought January feeders and sold June live cattle late, pit sources said.
